items.title: 'I Thought This Would Be Drama Free, How Wrong I Was' — Games Workshop Secured a £7.8 Million Refund on Donald Trump's Tariffs, but Iran War Threatens Supply Chain
items.description: The boss of Warhammer maker Games Workshop has said the company managed to secure a £7.8 million (approx. $10.3 million) refund on Donald Trump’s tariffs, but other issues, such as the Iran War, threaten its supply chain.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The boss of Warhammer maker Games Workshop has said the company managed to secure a £7.8 million (approx. $10.3 million) refund on Donald Trump’s tariffs, but other issues, such as the Iran War, threaten its supply chain.

The UK-based company makes the majority of its money through the sale of miniatures, which are painted by fans and used to play a variety of tabletop games, such as Warhammer 40,000. The U.S. is a significant market for Games Workshop, and so when Trump’s tariffs kicked in, the company was hit hard.

In its latest financial report, Games Workshop CEO Kevin Rountree said the company paid £12 million (approx. $15.9 million) in new U.S. tariffs during the last financial year. But following the U.S. Supreme Court ruling that declared the tariffs illegal, Games Workshop reclaimed £7.8 million of tariffs for the period to February 2026.

In February, the Supreme Court said Trump’s unprecedented use of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) was illegal. In early April last year, Trump held up a chart while speaking during a “Make America Wealthy Again” trade announcement event in the Rose Garden at the White House, and declared “Liberation Day.” The announcement confirmed additional tariffs targeting goods imported to the U.S. The U.S. Customs and ‌Border Protection agency ‌said it collected ​about $166 billion in duties and deposits under the emergency tariffs imposed ‌by Trump.

But following the Supreme Court decision, Trump introduced a new 10% global tariff rate, which Rountree said would cost Games Workshop £13 million (approx. $17.2 million) in new U.S. tariffs this financial year.

“Well, I thought this would be drama free, how wrong I was,” Rountree said during prepared remarks. “The continuous hard work on efficiency gains to improve our gross margin has continued. Unlike some companies, we do not consider tariffs as an exceptional item, but rather part of the uncertainty of operating globally.” Those mitigation measures include price increases and operational changes (Games Workshop announced price rises last October).

Trump’s tariffs have also had a significant impact on the world of video games, with Nintendo suing the U.S. government and demanding a refund with interest. Nintendo recently insisted it was under no obligation to pass that money back to consumers — even though they paid higher prices for Switch 2 products. Presumably Games Workshop would have a similar view.

Speaking of uncertainty, Rountree said "conflicts around the world” threaten to disrupt Games Workshop’s supply chain. He also flagged higher plastic ​input costs, estimating a roughly £2 million hit from supply-chain disruption and inflationary pressures linked to volatility in global energy markets.

Still, the Warhammer boom shows no sign of slowing down. Games Workshop’s profit before tax rose 4.9% ​to a record £275.7 million (approx. $366 million) for the fiscal ​year ⁠ended May 31, driven by continued growth in the core Warhammer business. “‘Games Workshop and the Warhammer hobby are in great shape,” Rountree declared.

Photo by John Keeble/Getty Images.

items.title: After 15 Years, Resident Evil 5 Has Finally Been Dethroned as The Series' Best-Selling Game
items.description: After 15 years, Resident Evil 5 is no longer the highest-selling entry in Capcom's survival horror series, the publisher has revealed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
After 15 years, Resident Evil 5 is no longer the highest-selling entry in Capcom's survival horror series, the publisher has revealed.

New sales figures for the Resident Evil franchise show its sales crown has now been taken by the Resident Evil 2 remake, which has now shifted 19.75 million copies — enough to slip past Resident Evil 5's final total of 19.01 million.

These totals are interesting for several reasons. Firstly, the fact that Resi 5's sales have taken a decade and a half to topple says a lot about the huge excitement for that game when it initially arrived — riding on the coat tails of the beloved original Resi 4, despite ultimately being judged as nowhere near as good.

Secondly, these totals show that the Resident Evil series' back catalogue continues to sell really well. Capcom's Resident Evil 2 remake launched back in 2019 and is clearly still shifting copies (and has likely benefited from the subsequent launches of other Leon S. Kennedy-starring titles such as the Resi 4 remake and Resident Evil Requiem).

Speaking of the Resi 4 remake and Requiem, you might wonder where their sales are in all of this. Well, they are still selling brilliantly, too — and may yet both eclipse Resident Evil 2 to become the franchise's top sellers, given enough time.

Resident Evil Requiem has now sold 8 million copies, a figure that will undoubtedly rise far further as the game gets discounted over time and receives its highly-anticipated post-launch expansion. Resident Evil 4's remake, meanwhile, is now on an impressive 16 million copies sold.

All combined, the Resident Evil franchise has now sold a combined 213 million copies across all of its games — a figure which sees it edge past the 212 million total sales of Square Enix's Final Fantasy franchise, although these have not yet been updated for this financial quarter.

Other Capcom games selling well include new franchise Pragmata (now up to 2.51 million copies sold) and Monster Hunter: World which has now sold an astonishing 30.45 million copies.

Next up for the Resident Evil franchise is the launch of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie on September 16, before the arrival of Resident Evil Veronica sometime in 2027.

items.title: Marvel's Spider-Man 2 Update Adds Tom Holland's Brand New Day Spidey Suit
items.description: PlayStation 5 blockbuster Marvel's Spider-Man 2 has today been updated to add two new Spidey suits, including Tom Holland's new costume from Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
PlayStation 5 blockbuster Marvel's Spider-Man 2 has today been updated to add two new Spidey suits, including Tom Holland's new costume from Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

In celebration of this week's new Spider-Man film, the web-slinging PS5 sequel has been patched to v1.005.000, which adds two new Spidey designs, plus support for Enhanced PSSR on PlayStation 5 Pro, as well as Power Saver mode.

Sony first announced the PS5 Power Saver mode for certain games last year. When manually enabled, supported PS5 games will scale back performance and will allow your console to reduce its power consumption — a neat way to save on your energy bills and (slightly) cut down on your home's impact on the environment.

The Brand New Day suit is available in-game now, labelled as the "Fresh Start" suit. Also available is the Spider-Man costume from Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

It's a Brand New Day for Marvel's Spider-Man 2! 🕷️

Get TWO NEW SUITS for Peter Parker in today's update, including the Fresh Start and the Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls suits.

v1.005.000 also adds support for Enhanced PSSR on PS5 Pro and Power Saver mode! #SpiderMan2PS5 pic.twitter.com/ln63ra7DeW

— Insomniac Games (@insomniacgames) July 28, 2026

Marvel's Spider-Man 2 developer Insomniac Games has regularly kept its most recent Spidey game updated with new suits, so these additions don't come as a huge surprise — even if their arrival via a free update is very welcome. Next up from the studio is Marvel's Wolverine, due to arrive exclusively for PS5 on September 15.

And, of course, just hours remain until the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Officially due for release in theaters on July 31, previews begin tomorrow. Early reactions from press are already on social media — all of which are very positive — and the movie is now projected to be the biggest box office launch of the year so far. Keep an eye for IGN's official review soon.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Live-Action Link Actor Discusses The Legend of Zelda Movie, Says He Was Too Young to Play Breath of the Wild When It Launched
items.description: Link actor Benjamin Evan Ainsworth has discussed preparing for Nintendo's upcoming live-action The Legend of Zelda movie — and said he was too young to play Breath of the Wild when it originally debuted.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Link actor Benjamin Evan Ainsworth has discussed preparing for Nintendo's upcoming live-action The Legend of Zelda movie — and said he was too young to play Breath of the Wild when it originally debuted.

Ainsworth is currently 17 years old, while Breath of the Wild originally launched for Switch in 2017 — meaning he would have been just eight years old at the time.

"I remember vividly when Breath of the Wild came out — and it might show my age — but I remember being quite young at the time when it came out, and so I didn't have a Switch at the time," Ainsworth told GamesRadar. "And so, I was watching gamers play it, and watching playthroughs, essentially."

While still a teenager, Ainsworth already has a string of high-profile projects under his belt — such as Netflix horror The Haunting of Bly Manor, CBC sitcom Son of a Critch, and his recent addition to the cast of HBO's House of the Dragon.

While Ainsworth may not have played Breath of the Wild a decade ago, the actor has said he's now a Zelda fan has caught himself up on the "history" of the character and series in preparation for his role. (Hopefully Nintendo has given him a Switch 2?)

"Upon being fortunate enough to play this role, such an iconic character, going back and realizing the 40 years of legacy and history, and the varied tones, the varied stories, the varied renditions and vocal performances of this character as well," Ainsworth continued. "Yeah, I'm a big fan, and just really excited, because it was an awesome thing to shoot. New Zealand is a wonderful place. But yeah, can't say too much more."

Nintendo has kept many details of its Zelda movie under-wraps, with no word on its story, setting or characters beyond Link and Zelda, the latter of whom will be played by Bo Bragason. Filming in New Zealand has now wrapped, though some fans got a sneaky glimpse — and believe they spotted Succession actress Dichen Lachman in costume as Zelda's aide Impa. Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes director Wes Ball is helming the film, and has spoken previously about wanting to make a "serious" and "grounded" adaptation that feels "real" to audiences.

With less than a year to go until the movie's April 30, 2027 launch date, fans expect to hear much more about the film soon — perhaps this fall, when Nintendo gets around to marking the Zelda franchise's 40th anniversary with its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remaster.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Square Enix Dev Yoshi-P Says Final Fantasy 6, 8, and 9 Remakes Would Probably Have to Be Released in Four or Even Five Installments
items.description: At the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin on Sunday, Final Fantasy 14 director-producer Naoki “Yoshi-P” Yoshida invited Final Fantasy 7 Remake series director Naoki Hamaguchi to the stage for a chat. Over this 75-minute Naoki’s Room section, the two Final Fantasy devs discussed their motivations, upcoming FF7/FF14 crossover content, and the future of the series. However, one comment may have quashed fans’ hopes for Final Fantasy 6, Final Fantasy 8, or Final Fantasy 9 ever getting the remake treatment.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
At the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin on Sunday, Final Fantasy 14 director-producer Naoki “Yoshi-P” Yoshida invited Final Fantasy 7 Remake series director Naoki Hamaguchi to the stage for a chat. Over this 75-minute Naoki’s Room section, the two Final Fantasy devs discussed their motivations, upcoming FF7/FF14 crossover content, and the future of the series. However, one comment may have quashed fans’ hopes for Final Fantasy 6, Final Fantasy 8, or Final Fantasy 9 ever getting the remake treatment.

The talk of remaking other FF games came up when Hamaguchi named Final Fantasy 6 as a big influence on his life. “Final Fantasy 6 is the reason I wanted to work in the game industry and it will always have a special place in my heart," he said. He added that whenever he mentions this in interviews, it inevitably sparks hopes and headlines that Hamaguchi will remake FF6, something that he always has to deny.

Yoshida added, “I understand fans’ feelings. But please think about it." He then went on to explain why these remakes would be such a huge effort to develop and release.

"Final Fantasy 6 is an incredibly huge game, and the same goes for other titles like Final Fantasy 8 and Final Fantasy 9. Since Final Fantasy 7 Remake, I understand why people ask for these remakes. But if we did remake these other games, we would probably have to release them in four or even five installments.”

Some have taken Yoshida's comments here to pour cold water on the chances of further Final Fantasy remakes in the Final Fantasy7 remake style. They echo those Final Fantasy 6 director Yoshinori Kitase issued in 2024, when he sad a Final Fantasy 6 remake akin to that of Final Fantasy 7's could take around 20 years to complete.

Kitase said that because of the depth of Final Fantasy 6, with so much content and so many characters, it would take twice the length of Final Fantasy 7 Remake to develop and release.

Hamaguchi went on to shout-out the Final Fantasy Remake trilogy team for their dedication and for sticking with him for over 10 years of development. “Not only was it a matter of timing, I think it was a miracle that we were able to get these people who were willing to stick around and keep motivated to work on so many of these titles back-to-back,” he said. “So that’s why I can’t just say, ‘Yeah, I’ll remake FF6,’ as it's not quite that simple.”

At the end of the talk, Yoshida pointed out that after they had mentioned the difficulties of remaking FF6 and other titles, there were many comments from livestream viewers along the lines of, ‘I want this guy (Hamaguchi) to make Final Fantasy 17,’ which Yoshida described as “the highest praise you could get.” Hamaguchi replied: “Can I respond to that? If I do…” but Yoshida waved him away.

This promoted many excited comments from viewers as to what this meant and if we can take this to mean that Square Enix has already decided to make Final Fantasy 17. Some have even interpreted this as a sign that Hamaguchi may already be slated to work on Final Fantasy 17, but it seems pretty tenuous to assume that, especially considering he still has his hands full with the upcoming Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.

Yoshida then asked Hamaguchi for both his most difficult and most rewarding experiences working on the Final Fantasy franchise. As a manager with a huge team of people, Hamaguchi said the most difficult thing is to unite everyone behind the same vision for the game and make sure they are heading in the same direction. According to Hamaguchi, the most rewarding thing is being able to make these games with the support of such a huge, global fanbase. “I don’t think anything could make me happier," he added.

Looking back on his career, Hamaguchi reminisced about how he spent ages fine-tuning fire effects on Final Fantasy 12 when he first started out as a programmer at Square Enix 24 years ago. “As an individual creator, it’s very satisfying to get immersed in your work. However, I think that’s something you’re able to do more earlier in your career. Later on, the satisfaction comes more from leading a team and getting them to utilize their abilities.” he explained. “This doesn’t change how I feel about the games. I still want to make something amazing.”

Yoshida and Hamaguchi then turned their attention to the new FF7-themed content coming to FF14 that their teams are collaborating on. This includes the Keybound Brawler game coming to FF14’s Golden Saucer in October, plus new Barret and Tifa-style outfits. The teams are currently working on the crossover raid Beyond the Lifestream, which will bring the FF7 remake series to FF14. It’s scheduled to come out with version 8.01 of Final Fantasy 14 (release date TBC, but set to drop before Final Fantasy 7 Revelations comes out in early 2027).

Regarding Final Fantasy 7, Hamaguchi reiterated that the whole reason they started the remake trilogy was to bring FF7 to the next generation of players, many of whom never experienced the 1997 PS1 classic. “We want to introduce new players to Final Fantasy 7 in a way that they can really understand what made the original so great. So we went into more depth on the depiction of the world, the lore, characters and all these elements in the remake trilogy," he said.

Throughout the talk, both developers praised each other for their respective work and achievements, revealing they don’t need much sleep and are still enthusiastic and committed to the Final Fantasy series. Yoshida praised Hamaguchi as being the number one at Square Enix in terms of team, task and schedule management. Towards the end of the talk, Hamaguchi expressed hopes that he and Yoshida’s teams can collaborate more in the future.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

Throughout the talk, both developers praised each other for their respective work and achievements, revealing they don’t need much sleep and are still enthusiastic and committed to the Final Fantasy series. Yoshida praised Hamaguchi as being the number one at Square Enix in terms of team, task and schedule management. Towards the end of the talk, Hamaguchi expressed hopes that he and Yoshida’s teams can collaborate more in the future.

items.title: Henry Cavill's Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe Finally Gets a Meaningful Update as Games Workshop Makes Significant Amazon Announcements
items.description: Games Workshop has made a number of significant announcements on the Henry Cavill Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe, as well as new Amazon animations based on its tabletop games.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Games Workshop has made a number of significant announcements on the Henry Cavill Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe, as well as new Amazon animations based on its tabletop games.

After concluding negotiations with Amazon to create Warhammer 40,000 movies and TV shows in December 2024, Games Workshop has now finally provided an update on the progress of the project. In a financial report, Games Workshop CEO Kevin Rountree said that Amazon had brought onboard United Artists (UA) and Mike Flannigan, who, having completed initial outlines, “should soon be moving on to script.”

Vertigo and Warhammer 40,000 superfan Henry Cavill “remain involved as they have been for some time,” Rountree added, which will come as some relief to those who took the radio silence around the project as a sign that Cavill may have exited his role as steward and star.

What happens next? Well, it sounds like it will still be some time before we get firm details on the setting and characters, if work hasn't even begun on a script. And we don’t yet know if Flanagan’s work relates to a movie or a TV show. Rountree did say that “UA have been decisive and brought their renowned pace and quality to the project,” though, so hopefully news will start to pick up.

What does the decision to bring Flanagan in tell us about what to expect? He’s best known for horror, having created the Netflix shows The Haunting of Hill House, The Haunting of Bly Manor, and Midnight Mass, among others. He’s also behind the upcoming Amazon Prime Video series Carrie, and wrote the first draft of the script for the upcoming DC Universe film Clayface.

So, it stands to reason that whatever this Warhammer 40,000 TV show or film is, it leans into horror. If that’s true it could be hugely exciting for fans. The grimdark 41st millennium is most famous for bombastic battles between Space Marines and terrifying aliens and demons, but Warhammer 40,000 has plenty about it that can be considered horror — even body horror, with the horrible Death Guard rotting themselves and everything around them.

Cavill, in a recent interview with Esquire, touched on the “complexity” and “trickiness” of adapting the Warhammer 40,000 IP. But, he insisted, he was loving the challenge. Bringing Warhammer to life "is a dream come true," Cavill said, "but it's different from what I've done before, in the sense I haven't had my hand on the tiller of things before. It's wonderful doing that. It is a tricky IP, and a very complex IP, and that's what I love about it. The challenges that come with putting this on the page in a way that is doing justice to that complexity, that trickiness, and that nuance, is a challenge I'm enjoying enormously."

When the Games Workshop / Amazon deal was announced, Cavill issued a statement on Instagram saying he’d been “working away in concept rooms, breaking down approaches to the enormity and magnificence of the Warhammer world."

He added: "together, we've been sifting through the plethora of incredible characters and poring over old tomes and texts. Our combined efforts have led us to a fantastic place to start our Universe, which has been agreed upon by those up on high at both Amazon and Games Workshop. That starting place shall, for now, remain a secret. Watch this space, though — more to come in time!"

Who might Cavill play across the Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe? Talking to IGN in 2021, Cavill expressed interest in playing one of the Primarchs or Captain-Generals, who are high-ranking key characters from the Warhammer lore.

Does the Amazon project need to be more grounded than a big galactic epic? We’re left with scraps to mull over, such as recent comments from Dan Abnett about NDAs and upcoming books.

The news doesn’t stop there, because Games Workshop also announced that it has almost completed an episode for Season 2 of Amazon’s animated anthology series, Secret Level, following the success of the Warhammer 40,000 episode in Season 1. This one, though, is set in the Warhammer: Age of Sigmar universe (fantasy). So don’t expect a follow-up to Titus’ adventures ahead of the release of Space Marine 3.

Fear not, because Games Workshop announced it has begun work on a full animated Warhammer 40,000 series featuring the Deathwatch. This series will be written by John Orloff, with Blur again animating, and released through Amazon. “We can’t wait to see it!” Rountree said.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: With Just Hours to Go Until Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Ryan Reynolds Says His New Monochrome Deadpool Suit is Actually Colored 'Jean Grey'
items.description: Amid huge speculation over Sadie Sink's character in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Deadpool star Ryan Reynolds has posted a cheeky nod to X-Men character Jean Grey via social media.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Amid huge speculation over Sadie Sink's character in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Deadpool star Ryan Reynolds has posted a cheeky nod to X-Men character Jean Grey via social media.

Reynolds appeared in-character during Marvel's San Diego Comic Con 2026 Marvel panel this past weekend to help promote Avengers: Doomsday and to show off a new grey-colored version of his superhero suit.

Now, Reynolds has posted what he claims is the exact color shade of this new suit — "Jean Grey" — and stated that "once you see it, you can't unsee it."

Once you see it, you can’t unsee it. pic.twitter.com/rfqw4YqPcY

— Ryan Reynolds (@VancityReynolds) July 27, 2026

For Marvel fans, this is an obvious nod to the ongoing discussion over the identity of Sadie Sink's Marvel role, which will finally be revealed this week when she debuts in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. But has Reynolds given the game away, or is this all just another of Deadpool's jokes?

To be clear, there is no actual "Jean Grey" color in paint company Pantone's range (we checked). And fans will already know that the color's fictional color code, 9-1963, is a nod to September 1963, when Stan Lee and Jack Kirby's original The X-Men #1 comic was published.

All of that said, if Reynolds has teased Jean Grey and this isn't who Sadie Sink is playing... well, it would be the exact sort of joke we'd expect. (Remember, also, that Tom Holland has insisted Jean Grey is "not in this movie." We'll see, eh!)

Last year, it was reported that Sink will be back in 2027's climactic Multiverse Saga finale Avengers: Secret Wars, something that seemingly sets her up for a far bigger MCU role. Of course, Marvel is currently prepping its big X-Men reboot, which is being helmed by Thunderbolts/The New Avengers director Jake Schreier. Introducing Jean Grey now would allow Marvel to gently introduce audiences to the idea of a fresh generation of X-Men, before fans get to say farewell to various legacy characters who are returning for Avengers: Doomsday.

Speaking on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Sink discussed the huge amount of secrecy over her role and described not being able to say who she's playing as "torture." Subsequent trailers have kept Sink in the shadows, though she has now begun giving interviews on Spider-Man: Brand New Day's promotional tour, with rather amusingly tight-lipped results. Beyond a marketing tactic to get fans speculating, director Destin Daniel Cretton has insisted that fans will ultimately appreciate being kept in suspense, and stated that Marvel was keeping the identity of Sadie Sink's character a secret until fans see the movie for a "very real reason" that he believes fans won't "get mad at."

Spider-Man: Brand New Day officially launches in theaters on July 31, though previews begin around the world in less than 24 hours. Early reactions from press are already on social media — all of which are very positive — and the movie is now projected to be the biggest box office launch of the year so far.

One thing you won't see in the movie when it launches is a cameo from recurring Marvel actress (and Ahsoka star) Rosario Dawson, who filmed a scene in-character as Clare Temple that has very sadly now been cut. Oh, and if you live in India, there's an 8-second moment you also won't see, due to an unusual decision about censorship.

Image credit: Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney

items.title: Xbox Executive Explains Outage, Vows to 'Do Better'
items.description: Xbox's Chief Technology Officer, Scott Van Vliet, has offered transparency and an explanation for the system and service outage that affected game libraries, sign-in, and game launching for many players from late Sunday night and well into Monday, vowing to "do better."
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Xbox's Chief Technology Officer, Scott Van Vliet, has offered transparency and an explanation for the system and service outage that affected game libraries, sign-in, and game launching for many players from late Sunday night and well into Monday, vowing to "do better."

In a post on X, Van Vliet attributed the issue to a failure of "a licensing service that sits outside of Xbox, but which Xbox depends upon." He did not name the service, but said it was "an internal service at Microsoft that is shared across multiple products, not some random system." He continued: "This caused some sign-in scenarios to fail, and it caused many scenarios that require an entitlement check to also fail, such as listing out your Full Library and launching games that you own," he continued. "It also affected several of our publishing and store partners who depend on those same systems which is why some of you saw issues in specific games and not others." He called it "an unacceptable situation" and that Xbox "must do better to support you."

To address the problem, the Xbox CTO said, "Our on-call teams caught the first signals overnight through automated monitoring and declared a major incident. Once we isolated the failing infrastructure, we shifted traffic onto the healthy parts of the system while the team continued to work towards a root cause. Service came back unevenly across regions which is why some of you recovered hours before others."

Van Vliet said that for the company's next step, "We're running a full post-incident review. I care less about the one-line root cause and more about the real questions: why a failure in one service was able to take down this much, why recovery took as long as it did, and what we change so a single point of failure can't ruin your night again. That means hardening the dependencies underneath sign in and game launch, improving how we detect and contain this class of failure, and being faster and clearer with you when something breaks."

He concluded by thanking Xbox gamers for their patience, and said, "We'll do better."

This incident follows PlayStation suffering its own prolonged system and service outage, while Xbox prepares for this week's wide launch of Halo: Campaign Evolved, the Unreal Engine 5-based remake and 25th anniversary celebration of the original Xbox's killer app. IGN gave Campaign Evolved a 7 out of 10 in our review.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of both IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, as well as our semi-retired interview show, IGN Unfiltered. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Is Projected to Have the Biggest Opening of 2026
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is on track to absolutely obliterate the box office this weekend.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is on track to absolutely obliterate the box office this weekend.

Various box office analysts have begun to release their projections for Spider-Man: Brand New Day's opening weekend at the box office, and in case there was any doubt, it's going to make heaps of money. Just two weeks after Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey set a high bar for a movie starring Tom Holland, Zendaya, and Jon Bernthal, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is expected to clear that bar with ease.

On the lower end of box office projections, Deadline estimates the film will make a whopping $180 - $190 million domestically on opening weekend. This would blow past Toy Story 5's $159 million domestic opening with ease and make Spidey the biggest opening of the year so far. Deadline noted that The Odyssey's continued legs and exclusive ownership of IMAX screens could put a dent in its potential earnings, but it will still dominate regardless thanks to other premium large format screens such as Dolby.

Box Office Pro, on the other hand, is projecting that Brand New Day will bring in $230M – $250M during its domestic opening weekend. This would be the second biggest opening in Spider-Man's cinematic history, with No Way Home holding the record at $260 million domestic. Another projection from a Twitter account known as Global Box Office estimates that globally, the film could amass $800 million in its opening weekend thanks to a massive international haul. That would make it the second biggest opening in history behind Avengers: Endgame, which pulled in a jaw-dropping $1.2 billion in its opening weekend.

That may be a stretch given the absurd build-up and unprecedented success of Avengers: Endgame, but if any character could come close, it would be Spider-Man. Regardless of where it lands, it certainly looks like Spider-Man: Brand New Day is going to help extend a massively successful summer for theaters and set a record for the year. It's unlikely any other film is going to match the commercial success of Spider-Man until Avengers: Doomsday, and even then, the popularity of a standalone Spider-Man adventure may outmatch the hype for a new Avengers film in 2026.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Is the Only MCU Movie in 2027 as Kevin Feige Promises Quality Over Quantity
items.description: It looks like Avengers: Secret Wars will be the only MCU movie in 2027, as Kevin Feige has promised that Marvel Studios is committed to "focusing on quality."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
It looks like Avengers: Secret Wars will be the only Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) movie in 2027, as Kevin Feige has promised that Marvel Studios is committed to "focusing on quality."

When Marvel stepped off the Hall H stage at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026, attendees in-person and at home were surprised to see Feige's crew come and go without mentioning any additional 2027 projects. Those keeping their MCU movie calendar updated will note that leaves the dates between Avengers: Doomsday's premiere on December 18, 2026, and Secret Wars' premiere on December 17, 2027, completely vacant.

It's a 12-month drought – one of Marvel Studios' longest ever – as the superhero universe paves the way for a potentially universe-ending conclusion to Phase Six late next year. In an interview with Empire, the Marvel Studios boss clarified that the studio has a good reason for leaving its post-Doomsday schedule open.

"A lot of it is a strategy we've talked about for a while, of focusing on quality," Feige explained. "We always try to focus on quality, but when quantity is so much, you get spread thin. We didn't want to be spread thin, and the Avengers is as important as it comes."

It's an update to the Marvel Studios strategy it's talked about in the past. Viewers have spent the 2020s attributing their "superhero fatigue" to a release schedule that has previously seen as many as four movies released in a single calendar year (and that doesn't count all of the TV shows). To help ease the pressure, Disney announced in 2024 that it would be slowing down its releases to just two or three movies, and two TV shows per year.

That same year happened to be one of the few with a single MCU movie premiere thanks to Deadpool & Wolverine's arrival in July. Still, its release followed just eight months after 2023's The Marvels. Captain America: Brave New World then arrived less than seven months later in February 2025.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day will end its own 12-month drought when it follows Fantastic Four: First Steps this Friday, July 31. Then, for the next year and a half, it's all about the Avengers.

Feige reiterated the importance of Secret Wars in particular, calling it "a setup in and of itself to the future, to what's next." Though he's adamant that it's not an MCU reboot, he added, "So really, it was landing those two movies and setting up 2028, of which we’ve revealed two of them so far, Ghost Rider and Panther III.”

The two MCU movies were maybe the biggest announcements from the SDCC Hall H panel. Highlights include Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider and David Jonsson as the next Black Panther. The former remains without a release date beyond its 2028 promise, with the latter set for December 15 of that year.

While the MCU will test die-hard fans' patience in 2027, moviegoers won't be entirely without theatrical releases from Marvel. So long as everything goes according to plan, Sony's Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse should help with the wait when it premieres June 18, 2027. On the TV side of things, Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is slated for a 2027 release.

We'll get to see just how painful the wait will be when Avengers: Doomsday arrives this December. Until then, you can freshen up on everything Marvel has in the pipeline. You can also check out everything else announced at the Hall H panel.

That same year happened to be one of the few with a single MCU movie premiere thanks to Deadpool & Wolverine's arrival in July. Still, its release followed just eight months after 2023's The Marvels. Captain America: Brave New World then arrived less than seven months later in February 2025.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day will end its own 12-month drought when it follows Fantastic Four: First Steps this Friday, July 31. Then, for the next year and a half, it's all about the Avengers.

Feige reiterated the importance of Secret Wars in particular, calling it "a setup in and of itself to the future, to what's next." Though he's adamant that it's not an MCU reboot, he added, "So really, it was landing those two movies and setting up 2028, of which we’ve revealed two of them so far, Ghost Rider and Panther III.”

The two MCU movies were maybe the biggest announcements from the SDCC Hall H panel. Highlights include Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider and David Jonsson as the next Black Panther. The former remains without a release date beyond its 2028 promise, with the latter set for December 15 of that year.

While the MCU will test die-hard fans' patience in 2027, moviegoers won't be entirely without theatrical releases from Marvel. So long as everything goes according to plan, Sony's Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse should help with the wait when it premieres June 18, 2027. On the TV side of things, Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is slated for a 2027 release.

We'll get to see just how painful the wait will be when Avengers: Doomsday arrives this December. Until then, you can freshen up on everything Marvel has in the pipeline. You can also check out everything else announced at the Hall H panel.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops Fans Discover Cut Zombies Content Over 15 Years After Release
items.description: Call of Duty: Black Ops fans have uncovered a new cut Zombies mode from the game, over a decade and a half after its original release.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Call of Duty: Black Ops fans have uncovered a new cut Zombies mode from the game, over a decade and a half after its original release.

YouTuber JTAG uncovered a tower defense Zombies mode in the recent PS4 port of Black Ops 1 and uploaded gameplay of it. It's clearly unfinished, so the mode is a bit crude, but players would've been able to place down turrets to stop hordes of the undead from advancing through a maze-like map. It seems as though the player would've been able to look down at the action from a bird's-eye view, not unlike Bloons Tower Defense, but they also would've been able to get on the ground and shoot enemies just like regular Call of Duty.

It's possible this was scrapped in favor of Dead Ops Arcade, a hidden Zombies mode in the original Black Ops game. The mode was a twin-stick arcade shooter that players could access by using a secret computer terminal in the main menu of Black Ops. The mode became a cult-classic and has returned in various Black Ops titles over the year.

Treyarch has experimented with the Zombies formula a lot over the years, and it's not exactly a surprise to see something like this turn up. The original Zombies mode was made by a small team of passionate developers who were developing the project in secret. It wasn't officially sanctioned by Activision and used recycled assets from Call of Duty: World at War. There was zero guarantee it would even make it into the final game, but once the team presented it to executives, they realized it was special and worth tacking on. And now, it's one of the most beloved pieces of the Call of Duty franchise.

It wouldn't be surprising if this tower defense mode was one of many experiments done to try and find more weird ways to expand the mode. It seems unlikely it will ever return, but it's cool to have a peek behind the curtain, especially when it's remained a secret for such a long time and may have never been discovered if not for the recent ports.

items.title: Ubisoft Gives Free PC Copies to Xbox Owners of Select Games
items.description: Ubisoft is giving Xbox owners free access to some of their games on PC.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Ubisoft is giving Xbox owners free access to some of their games on PC.

Today, Ubisoft and Xbox revealed a new expansion to their ongoing partnership. Starting immediately, those who own the following games on Xbox will get them for free on PC through Ubisoft Connect by August 4th:

  • Assassin’s Creed Mirage
  • Assassin’s Creed Valhalla
  • Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora
  • Far Cry 6
  • Immortals Fenyx Rising
  • Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown
  • Riders Republic
  • Skull and Bones
  • The Crew 2
  • The Crew Motorfest
  • Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Extraction
  • Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Siege

The games should appear in your Ubisoft Connect library by next week, so long as your accounts are linked. If you happen to purchase these games on Xbox later, you will get them on PC automatically. Unfortunately, this doesn't go both ways. If you buy one of these games on PC first, you will not get it on Xbox. If you're someone who previously played on console, but made the jump to PC, this is a great benefit.

Additionally, Ubisoft has also added a bunch of premium editions for Ubisoft games like Assassin's Creed Shadows to Xbox's PC app. Recently, Xbox has been making a lot of moves toward PC. It's unclear if this is all part of one big deliberate plan or if it's coincidental, but last week, Xbox made select backward-compatible titles for the OG Xbox available on PC. More titles are expected to be added in the future.

There are also rumors that Microsoft is planning a feature that will let players digitize their physical games library, possibly ahead of the next Xbox console. However, with this ongoing shift toward PC, it could make them accessible on PC. It's believed the next Xbox is expected to be more PC-like, so this could all be part of one big initatitve to prepare for the next-generation of Xbox.

items.title: The Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Beta Proves Fans Still Really Want That Blade Movie
items.description: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is coming off a record-breaking open beta weekend, where two particular characters reigned supreme over the rest of the game’s cast.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is coming off a record-breaking open beta weekend, where two particular characters reigned supreme over the rest of the game’s cast.

Despite some glaring issues that plagued PC users, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls still had a massively successful open beta, raking in more players on Steam than any other fighting game’s open beta before it.

Specifically, Marvel Tokon attracted 33,233 players at its all-time peak, just under 500 more than Street Fighter 6’s famously packed beta back in 2023. For reference, that number was 32,787, while, for comparison’s sake, Tekken 8’s open beta garnered 15,035 players later that same year.

Of those players, a significant portion of them chose two characters more than any others. Those characters are Magick and Blade, respectively, with Magick being the consistent leader of the two. As seen in stats presented by the FGC’s resident data-compiler and infographic creator AlietteFaye, character usage in Vibranium ranks and above saw an overwhelming majority using Magick overall, as well as using her as a Team Leader.
Blade wasn’t far behind, ranking as the second most-used character overall. His position fell to fourth when it came to Team Leaders, with Spidey and Shuri in second and third place, though he was by far the most popular Assist Character out of the lot. Magick still maintained her popularity in this regard, coming in second as an Assist.

Magneto and Spider-Man were Tokon’s third and fourth-most popular picks, both in overall usage and as Assist characters, while on the other end of the lineup, Danger was consistently the least popular character in all aspects. Miss Marvel was just ahead of her in overall usage and assists, but was far more popular as a Team Leader.

A final look at the character usage in Vibranium and above during Tokon's open beta.
Data was taken just before the servers went down!

(Pray that Arcsys makes the leaderboards a bit easier to navigate/filter so that I can do more detailed breakdowns.)#MARVELTOKON #MARVELTōkon pic.twitter.com/atAQytKGhI

— AlietteFaye | Day -232 Ryu Hater (@AlietteFaye) July 27, 2026

While this data was only compiled within the game’s highest ranks, it certainly reflects many of the matches we saw over the weekend. You couldn’t go online without seeing a Magick or a Blade, a trend that speaks to their popularity within the broader gaming community.

It’s little surprise that Blade was one of the most-used characters during the open beta. Fans have been pining for another Blade movie and video game for ages now, with Marvel President Kevin Feige recently admitting he felt like a “gigantic loser and failure” for not getting the Mahershala Ali flick off the ground after seven years.

The Daywalker’s game adaptation is also in peril, with Xbox looking to either sell or close Arkane, the studio responsible for its development, in the thick of Microsoft’s massive restructuring efforts.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said the development house "is beginning required consultation with its Works Council to review potential strategic options,” leaving fans hopeful that there is some light at the end of the tunnel for a Blade game.

For now, players have Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls to look forward to, which releases on August 6, 2026. Marvel's Wolverine isn't far behind either, releasing in September 15, 2026 for the PlayStation 5.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: The Odyssey Translator Unleashes Scathing Review of Christopher Nolan's Film Adaptation
items.description: Greek translator and University of Pennsylvania professor Emily Wilson has unleashed a scathing review of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, calling it a "confused" and "abysmal" adaptation of Homer's text.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Greek translator and University of Pennsylvania professor Emily Wilson has unleashed a scathing review of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, calling it a "confused" and "abysmal" adaptation of Homer's text.

Wilson took to the London Review of Books to publish a lengthy assessment of Nolan's blockbuster epic and how, at least for her, it failed (via The Guardian). Her review began simply enough, praising The Odyssey as an easy-to-follow tale that her "teenagers had a good time" with, but her positivity mostly ends about one paragraph in.

"It's a family-friendly audiovisual spectacle," Wilson said, "like an elaborate Fourth of July fireworks display – and with about the same level of narrative and emotional depth."

Ouch. Wilson's thoughts on Nolan's latest movie only heat up from there.

"But the film's vision is too confused, its characters too underdeveloped, to deliver what it half-promises in terms of big ideas – although it is very good at conveying big bangs and big giants," she added.

It's unclear if Nolan, an infamously phoneless filmmaker, has had time to digest Wilson's thoughts on his work, but he might have his feelings hurt if he has. The director referenced Wilson's translation of the Greek story when speaking with Empire late last year, so he's certainly familiar with her work.

Wilson's full review doesn't mark her first foray into the topic of this year's The Odyssey. Last week, she criticized the film for its changes to the source material, saying she was concerned Nolan "was trying to pack everything in while missing themes that were essential to the poem." Her review allowed her to elaborate on some of the elements she found to be particularly bothersome.

"But I would be ashamed to have written any part of this script," Wilson said, calling back to Nolan citing her work. "Sadly, Damon's Odysseus isn't complicated or wily or artful."

She continued later in her piece: "Nolan's Odyssey lacks many of the elements that make the poem great. It has nothing convincing to say about time, memory, history, war, or about the relationship between one warrior's glorious return and the lives of his family, adversaries, comrades, friends and neighbors. It lacks psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth. Its narrative structure is gimmicky. The writing is abysmal. None of the characters has convincing motivation for their actions or words. There are no sex scenes, and all the food looks horrible."

Wilson signed off on one bright note: The Odyssey is convincing audiences to go back to movie theaters. She's celebrated the idea that a big-budget movie had managed to ignite interest in Homer's work for a new audience before, and it's still something she's happy to see today.

"Perhaps the film will persuade a few college administrators not to cut their literature, language, and history departments," she explained. "Nolan, who studied English at University College London – where students still study The Odyssey as a first year 'foundational text' – is doing his best to get the general public reading again, and I am grateful."

Wilson has an undeniably deeper relationship with Homer's work than the average moviegoer, but that hasn't stopped the army of fans who have turned up in theaters to see what Nolan's latest is all about. With solid reviews (we gave it an 8/10) and good word-of-mouth, The Odyssey has seen enormous success at the box office. Its opening weekend brought in $264.1 million globally, while its second weekend, with only a 19% drop, accumulated another $215.3 million.

For more, you can read what Nolan had to say about the changes he made to the story. You can also see what Universal did to stop the flow of leaks that popped up online over the weekend.

items.title: 'I Can't Not Hear His Voice in My Head' — Matt Dinniman Reflects on Writing Dungeon Crawler Carl With Jeff Hays in Mind
items.description: "I think Fuzzy Door would have a riot on their hands if they hadn't cast Jeff in something," said Dinniman during an SDCC interview with IGN. "He's so associated with that sound and that voice. Anybody else would be jarring."
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl books started as just another LitRPG series, but have recently started exploding into a major franchise. Its rapid acceleration into the mainstream is mostly due to Matt Dinniman's fantastic story, but it's also very tied to the success of the audiobooks and the incredible voices of narrator Jeff Hays.

The Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks are some of the best audiobooks you can listen to right now, and that's thanks to Hays bringing key characters to life. With the official TV adaptation on the horizon, it's unsurprising that Hays was officially cast to play the role of Princess Donut.

"I think Fuzzy Door would have a riot on their hands if they hadn't cast Jeff in something," said Dinniman during an SDCC interview with IGN. "He's so associated with that sound and that voice. Anybody else would be jarring."

While Jeff Hays' Princess Donut voice is certainly iconic (and now included in a flash game), it's only one small part of the larger casting choices Fuzzy Door Studios will have to make. For those who have only experienced Dungeon Crawler Carl via audio, there are literally hundreds of character voices that audiences now associate with Hays' interpretation.

"I can't not hear his voice in my head whenever I write," said Dinniman about Hays. "He does such a good job encapsulating the characters that I don't need to change anything in order to match the voice."

Jeff Hays is the first official casting choice for the Dungeon Crawler Carl TV series and it's still very early days in terms of production. It was only recently confirmed this year that the adaptation would be coming to Peacock, but we do know that the series is going to be live-action instead of animated. With Hays officially cast as Princess Donut, it's definitely possible he'll be pulled into other roles that will rely heavily on CGI to be brought to the screen.

"I'm excited that I'm going to have a part in helping the TV show be just a little bit better," said Hays about his role. "I was like, 'Look, just give me that one and you know, do what you want with the rest.'"

Although we don't have any sort of release date set for the TV show, the eighth book was just published earlier this year for both print and audio. If you haven't already read the series, there's plenty of time to catch up before the adaptation comes to streaming.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics -- from TV series to books and the latest Pokémon games.

items.title: House of the Dragon: Rhaenyra’s Worst Omen Yet Foreshadows the ‘Rot That Follows’
items.description: House of the Dragon: Season 3’s sixth episode depicts a moment that its director called “an instigating event for a lot of bad things” to come in the series. “That cut on Rhaenyra's finger becomes an instigating event for a lot of bad things,” director Loni Peristere declared in HBO’s Inside the Episode featurette.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Spoilers ahead for the latest episode of House of the Dragon.

House of the Dragon: Season 3’s sixth episode, “Faceless Men”, depicts a moment that its director called “an instigating event for a lot of bad things” to come in the series.

As a frustrated Rhaenyra hears petitions from her complaining subjects, she cuts her finger on the Iron Throne, something that also happened to her father, King Viserys I, and proved a bad omen for him personally and for his reign.

“That cut on Rhaenyra's finger becomes an instigating event for a lot of bad things,” director Loni Peristere declared in HBO’s Inside the Episode featurette.

“One of the greatest scenes in the series is the moment that Rhaenyra cuts her finger on the iron throne. We all know what that means,” Peristere explained. “There's infections that follow. There's rot that follows. It basically reveals what's ultimately happening for real in Rhaenyra's tenure as queen.”

Rhaenyra actor Emma D’Arcy added: “There's obviously some significant foreshadowing in this moment. Though I don't know to what extent Rhaenyra is cognizant of its significance. Viserys kept his own condition very private. I don't know how she could know that the throne was the root of his illness. I think Rhaenyra perceives it is part of kind of broader hostility. I think she experiences the throne and the crown and the council, the sort of vestiges of leadership as hostile in some way.”

House of the Dragon showrunner Ryan Condal views the cut as representative of Rhaenyra being “torn between the old principles of Daemon and the new progressive principles of Viserys. It was more of a symbol to show the struggle that she is going through and to remind her that Viserys looms very large in her life.”

The “rot that follows” Peristere warned of is almost immediately evident when Rhaenyra orders Alicent to kill her own son, Rhaenyra’s archenemy Aemond, if she wants better treatment for her and her daughter Helaena.

Helaena’s pregnancy certainly is a challenge to Rhaenyra’s rule and, in the words of Condal, makes both mother and unborn child “expendable” to the queen:

“It puts Rhaenyra in a really terrible spot. And this brings her back to all these existential questions as to how she’s gonna be able to win her throne in a way that she doesn’t completely compromise her moral standing.”

Rhaenyra may soon find herself left with little choice but to do the unthinkable in order to preserve her rule and end the civil war.

The episode’s co-writer, David Hancock, warned that Rhaenyra’s ambition to defeat Ormund Hightower while growing neglectful of her subjects could lead her to make a terrible strategic miscalculation: “If she kills indiscriminately, subjects loyal to her might well rise up in insurrection. items.title: YouTube Premium Is Adding a Peacock Subscription at No Extra Cost
items.description: YouTube Premium is becoming an even better value, as the service will soon include a subscription to Peacock at no extra cost for users in the United States.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
YouTube Premium is becoming an even better value, as the service will soon include a subscription to Peacock at no extra cost for users in the United States.

Starting early next year, YouTube Premium subscribers in the U.S. will get access to Peacock's ad-supported Premium tier. This means you'll be able to watch films like Obsession and Minions, TV shows like Ted and Twisted Metal, and have access to Peacock's NFL and NBA offerings all through YouTube. The news was confirmed today as part of a larger initiative to expand Peacock's reach.

“With this agreement, Peacock accelerates its next phase of growth by bringing the service to millions of YouTube Premium subscribers, driving long-term value for our business," said Matt Strauss, Chairman, Media Group, NBCUniversal. "Combined with our YouTube TV extension, this agreement opens the door to new ways for audiences to discover, access and deepen engagement with NBCUniversal's industry-leading content wherever and however they choose to watch.”

Although there is no additional cost factored into this, some are worried it could create some kind of price hike for YouTube Premium in the future. We've already seen how such massive increases in value can lead to issues long-term, resulting in eventual price hikes. Xbox, for instance, made Call of Duty available through Game Pass for two years, which eventually led to a price increase on the service.

Earlier this year, Microsoft revealed that Call of Duty would no longer be available on Game Pass on day one and lowered the price of the subscription. For now, though, YouTube Premium will remain at $15.99. Should the price remain unchanged, this is a pretty incredible deal, especially for sports fans. Peacock's ad-supported Premium plan itself normally costs $10.99, so there's a fair bit of savings for those who already make use of YouTube Premium.

As of right now, there's no concrete release date for this expansion, but it is targeting a release of early 2027.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Physical 'Copies' of GTA 6 Will Expire 170 Days After Launch Date in Japan
items.description: If you’re buying ‘physical’ copies of GTA 6 in Japan, you’d better act fast and download that code lickety-split, else it might expire while you’re not looking.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
If you’re buying ‘physical’ copies of GTA 6 in Japan, you’d better act fast and download that code lickety-split, else it might expire while you’re not looking.

Rockstar already ruffled some feathers after revealing that ‘physical’ copies of Grand Theft Auto 6 would be that in name only. You get a cool box, but a disc won’t be inside it; instead, you’ll get a digital download code, which, in some regions, will expire after a certain period of time has passed.

As spotted by Power Unlimited columnist ‘Genki,’ Rockstar’s official website states that physical editions of the game will expire in Japan 170 days after launch on November 19th, 2026, due to “regional regulations.”

UPDATE: It has been confirmed that in Japan the Grand Theft Auto VI physical version download code in a box WILL expire after 170 days due to regional regulations!

The reason is the Japan “Payment Services Act” that states companies selling prepaid payments must register and… https://t.co/pwDjh8yvfG pic.twitter.com/TJVpiP04kc

— Genki✨ (@Genki_JPN) July 27, 2026

While there was some initial confusion as to whether or not this only applied to separate codes for DLC content, it has since been confirmed that yes, the actual GTA 6 product code will expire if not claimed after 170 days within Japan.

Genki cited Japan’s Payment Services Act as the reason for this. It’s a strict law that aims to protect consumers from getting scammed, requiring sellers of digital codes to set aside large amounts of money in the event their companies go under or disappear from the market completely.

To no one’s surprise, most corporations don’t want to hand the Japanese Government tons of cash for indefinite safekeeping. Lucky for them, there’s a way to circumvent this; if the product expires in less than six months, the rule doesn’t apply, which is why these GTA 6 codes have an expiration date of 170 days.

Regardless of the intended financial protections, folks online aren’t too happy with this news, with one theorizing on X, “Guess they’ll need to refresh stock pretty regularly to avoid people buying an out-of-date code.”

“Yes, that or they don’t do anymore shipments after it is sold out,” Genki replied.

Rockstar’s decision to push codes in lieu of a fully physical disc for GTA 6 was hot on the heels of Sony’s announcement that it will stop printing game discs as of January 2028, sparking a heated debate around digital ownership that hasn’t shown any signs of slowing down.

In fact, nearly all of PlayStation’s recent social media posts have been inundated with angry comments from players protesting the platform’s controversial business move, with the latest trailer for Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil film getting flooded with jokes that the central character isn’t transporting an organ, but rather “the last physical game copy in existence.”

Players can’t help but fear that this signals a transition that will echo through the rest of the industry, leading to an all-digital future where games, movies, and more can be pulled at-will, despite consumers having paid for them.

Protesters are even suggesting a full PlayStation blackout, urging players not to use Sony’s services from August 23 - 30 as a way of showing the company they mean business. Whether or not it’ll actually happen, or prove effective, remains to be seen.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Shang-Chi Star Simu Liu Says He Would 'Crawl Through a Mile of Broken Glass' for a Sequel
items.description: We still know next to nothing about Shang-Chi 2, but star Simu Liu said he would "crawl through a mile of broken glass on my bare hands" to make it happen.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
We still know next to nothing about Shang-Chi 2, but star Simu Liu said he would "crawl through a mile of broken glass on my bare hands" to make it happen.

The Marvel actor explained the lengths he's willing to go to for a sequel to his 2021 superhero movie during an interview with Variety. As the Marvel Studios Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con came and went without any Shang-Chi 2 news, Liu took the opportunity to thank the fans who have been begging to see it made for the last five years.

"Your guess is as good as mine," he said when asked about the status of a follow-up. "Look, I will say this: The only reason why people even ask about a sequel is because there are so many incredible fans that loved the first one so much, and I will never ever stop being the most grateful for all of those people.

"I was reminded of it, yet again, when we were at Hall H. It was just such an atmosphere of joy. I mean, we had people waiting over 30 hours in line just to be there with us. I wanted to reach out and touch every single one of them just to say, 'Thank you.' They're the reason why I'm here and the reason why we're even throwing words like 'sequel' around."

Liu first appeared as Shaun/Shang-Chi when Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings came to theaters in 2021. Despite teasing some interesting connections to the greater Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), we've seen little of his character – or characters like Katy (Awkwafina) and Ying Nan (Michelle Yeoh) – since. Those wanting to see more from Liu in Marvel in the meantime would had to have caught him in animated projects like What If...? and Marvel Zombies.

The Shang-Chi drought in the MCU will at least change in a big way later this year. Liu's character is confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday when it premieres this December, with last week's trailer teasing that he'll be included in at least a few action scenes. Exactly how prominent his role will be in the film remains to be seen.

Fans think Liu and Shang-Chi deserve more. The actor said he'd be willing to shed some blood if it meant Shang-Chi 2 could become a reality sooner rather than later.

"Whenever and wherever the call comes, I would crawl through a mile of broken glass on my bare hands to do it," he added. "Because I know how much this movie means to me, but more importantly, I know how much it means to the fans that loved it."

Liu admitted it would be "preferable" if he didn't have to do the whole crawl-through-glass bit, but because Shang-Chi means so much to him, he's leaving everything on the table.

"I was hoping that would be taken metaphorically, but if it had to be literal, I would be open," he said.

Original director Destin Daniel Cretton, who is currently wrapped up as the filmmaker in charge of this week's Spider-Man: Brand New Day and released Marvel's Wonder Man show earlier this year, has at least given fans some hope that a sequel will soon materialize. While the when, where, and how remain a mystery, the director said Shang-Chi 2 is something Marvel is "working on."

"The first film's reception was incredible, and we want to honor that," Cretton said last month. "It's evolving in a way we're excited about."

Liu said in 2023 that his sequel was originally set to show up after the upcoming Avengers projects, but as delays kept pushing Marvel's plans back, plans for a follow-up for his standalone MCU had been impacted, too. The next year, he promised a sequel would arrive eventually, and in January of this year, he said that's still the plan.

For now, we'll have to wait to see how Liu will help take on Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom when Avengers: Doomsday premieres December 18, 2026. Until then, you can read about Ghost Rider, Black Panther 3, and all of the other announcements Marvel had to show off at its big Hall H SDCC panel this year.

Photo by Chris DELMAS / AFP via Getty Images.

items.title: William Gibson Speaks Out After Neuromancer Trailer Sparks Doubts Among Fans
items.description: William Gibson, author of the cyberpunk Bible Neuromancer, is putting fans’ fears to rest about Apple TV’s adaptation of his genre-defining novel.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
William Gibson, author of the cyberpunk Bible Neuromancer, is putting fans’ fears to rest about Apple TV’s long-awaited adaptation of his genre-defining novel.

Neuromancer’s first full-length trailer debuted at San Diego Comic Con 2026, and as expected, reactions were equal parts ecstatic and doubtful. Given that the book has gone without a proper adaptation since it was published in 1984, it’s had plenty of time to marinate in the hearts and minds of cyberpunks over the last forty years, and each fan has their own idea of how it ought to look.

An impassioned debate sprung up across social media the instant the trailer debuted online, leaving many divided about Apple’s casting choices (isn't Callum Turner just a bit too handsome to play Case?), as well as its overall tone and aesthetic translation of Gibson’s heavily-stylized vision of the future.

Fear not; Gibson, who also served as an executive producer for the show, says he’s been extremely pleased with how things went throughout the production process, as told in a concise post on his Bluesky profile.

“Anyone who doesn’t see how very satisfied I’ve been throughout production doesn’t get what I most want out of an adaptation. Mind you, that does tend to happen,” he wrote.

This follows his previous remarks about the adaptation back in 2024, where he broke down his contributions to the series — as well as gave a cheeky finger-wag to fans with their own expectations of how it should be.

“I answer [the] showrunner’s and director’s questions about the source material. I read drafts and make suggestions. And that’s it, really, though my previous experience has been that that winds up being quite a lot of work in itself,” he said in a tweet thread.

“I don’t have veto power. The showrunner and director do, because the adaptation’s their creation, not mine. A novel is a solitary creation. An adaptation is a fundamentally collaborative creation, so first of all isn’t going to ‘be the book.’ Particularly not the one you saw behind your forehead when you read the book, because that one is yours alone.”

It’s worth noting that Gibson has adapted his own work for the screen before, most notably writing the screenplay for Johnny Mnemonic… though his reaction to the final product was less than enthusiastic after studios ballooned its budget and made some baffling last-minute changes after Keanu Reeves became a massive Hollywood star following Speed’s success at the box office.

4) Particularly not the one you saw behind your forehead when you read the book, because that one is yours alone. So for now let’s leave it at that.

— William Gibson (@GreatDismal) February 29, 2024

Neuromancer is the latest big-budget adaptation of his work following Prime Video’s take on his 2014 novel The Peripheral, starring Chloe Grace Moretz. The series received mixed reviews, with IGN’s Tara Bennett giving it a 6 out of 10. Gibson, for his part, seemed fairly enthusiastic about the show, with executive producer Vicenzo Natali remarking that the author wasn’t exactly married to the idea of a 1:1 remake of his book.

"He loves what Jonathan and Lisa have done, and we've had this long-standing relationship, so I think he had a lot of confidence in the group. But never was possessive,” Natali said to SyFy. “If anything, he was inspiring and threw some of the more interesting new ideas that are not in the books at us that eventually were incorporated in the show. It's a very comfortable space to work in, because he makes it a safe space to adapt the work.”

Neuromancer is set to release Friday, January 22nd, 2027, exclusively on Apple TV.

Neuromancer is the latest big-budget adaptation of his work following Prime Video’s take on his 2014 novel The Peripheral, starring Chloe Grace Moretz. The series received mixed reviews, with IGN’s Tara Bennett giving it a 6 out of 10. Gibson, for his part, seemed fairly enthusiastic about the show, with executive producer Vicenzo Natali remarking that the author wasn’t exactly married to the idea of a 1:1 remake of his book.

"He loves what Jonathan and Lisa have done, and we've had this long-standing relationship, so I think he had a lot of confidence in the group. But never was possessive,” Natali said to SyFy. “If anything, he was inspiring and threw some of the more interesting new ideas that are not in the books at us that eventually were incorporated in the show. It's a very comfortable space to work in, because he makes it a safe space to adapt the work.”

Neuromancer is set to release Friday, January 22nd, 2027, exclusively on Apple TV.
